title: Telemetry-driven precision path planner for runtime mixed-precision selection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a telemetry-driven planner that chooses a per-request mixed-precision execution path (FP16 / FP8 / INT8) using compact cost+accuracy models and an online calibration corpus. The planner should: 1) use recent token- and request-level telemetry (latency distribution, token-error signals, model-version), 2) consult quantization profiles and calibration confidence scores, 3) compute an expected utility (latency-cost-accuracy tradeoff) per candidate path, and 4) pick a runtime path with graceful fallback to higher-precision when confidence is low. This ticket covers design, offline validation harness, runtime scheduler integration, and canary rollout policy for the new planner.
acceptance_criteria: Planner can be configured per-route and per-model with fallback thresholds and cost weights
Offline validator shows <=0.5% average task-level accuracy regression on canonical eval suites when using planner-selected paths vs baseline FP16, for recommended profiles
End-to-end telemetry pipeline feeds a 24h sliding window for planner decisions and updates quantization confidence scores every 6 hours
Canary rollout supports % traffic split and automatic rollback on accuracy SLA breach
Unit and integration tests covering path selection heuristics, calibration ingestion, and fallback logic
Performance: planner decision latency < 150us added to request path in hot path (configurable off-path sampling)
Docs: config schema, operator runbook, and example rollout strategy in Console docs
tasks: Design doc for precision path planner and scoring model (link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/runtime/precision-path-planner)
Build offline validation harness to replay calibration corpus and measure end-to-end accuracy + token-cost estimates
Implement compact scoring: combine latency model, token-cost model, and calibration-confidence into single utility score
Add telemetry ETL jobs to surface per-route token latency P50/P95/P99 and accuracy signals to Planner store
Integrate planner with runtime scheduler as a lightweight decision point; provide async sampling mode
Create canary rollout in Console with automatic rollback triggers and dashboards
Run grid of quant profiles (FP16/FP8/INT8 variants) on representative models and produce recommendation table
decisions: Use a lightweight linear utility model (weights configurable per-customer) vs a heavyweight ML model to keep production safety and explainability
Calibration corpus will be maintained via reservoir sampling of recent requests (privacy-filtered) plus curated prompt sets for critical customers
Planner will compute decisions synchronously for 90% of requests, with a sampling path that allows offline validation and telemetry without latency impact
Default policy: prefer lower precision when expected utility delta > configured margin; fallback to FP16 on confidence < threshold
tradeoffs: Explainability vs optimality: linear utility is interpretable but may miss complex interactions; acceptable for initial rollout
Sampling frequency vs telemetry staleness: 6h confidence refresh balances noise and responsiveness; can be tuned per-customer
Synchronous decision latency vs throughput: we avoid heavy models in hot path; heavy path decisions run off-path and update policy periodically
risks: Calibration corpus drift may cause silent accuracy regressions if not monitored
Telemetry gaps (e.g., missing token-level accuracy signals) could bias planner toward lower precision
Edge-case models with brittle INT8 behavior may require manual profile pinning
Rollback windows need to be conservative to avoid oscillation during traffic spikes
validation_plan: Offline: run full eval suite on 50k calibration samples across 6 representative models comparing baseline FP16 vs planner-selected paths
A/B canary: 1% traffic with planner enabled, compare quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/EM/LLR) and latency/cost for 48h
Stress tests: spike traffic with concurrent mixed-precision decisions to validate runtime scheduler and fallback paths
Regression alerts: wire up paging alerts if model-level accuracy drops >0.8% or latency P95 increases beyond SLO
observability: Expose per-path counters (chosen_path, fallback_count), per-model accuracy drift, and utility score histogram
Dashboard: path distribution, per-route cost delta, and calibration confidence over time
Tracing: add trace span for planner decision with decision inputs and selected path
Logs: sample decision logs to S3 for offline audit and replays
